`next-cursor` advances only when both of these conditions hold:

## Frames

(己, p=0.99) **A bounded read can advance while admitting fewer encounters than it fetched.** Intentional label exclusions and valid empty system rows do not themselves indicate a truncated read. A full page should retain `overflow? true` and `complete? false` while progressing.

(己, p=0.99) **Failed classification is a different outcome.** At [tools.cljs:156](/home/err/spaces/cephalon-local-character/knoxx/backend/src/cljs/knoxx/backend/domain/discord/tools.cljs:156), a label lookup exception becomes `[]`, which the caller reports as successful details. Adding raw IDs and advancing every such result would permanently skip otherwise eligible rows after a transient label-service failure. The repair needs a bounded failure distinction.

Discord documents newest-to-oldest response order and mutually exclusive pagination parameters. Its upstream Python iterator advances `after` from the newest returned ID, supporting full-page progression without treating a short page as a prerequisite. This is documentation/source corroboration, not a live Knoxx observation. [Discord endpoint contract](https://github.com/discord/discord-api-docs/blob/main/developers/resources/message.mdx#get-channel-messages), [upstream iterator](https://github.com/Rapptz/discord.py/blob/master/discord/abc.py).

## Countermoves

(己, p=0.99) Safe cursor preconditions for this adapter are:

- Exact authorized owner/account/channel binding and successful read/classification.
- Known integral `rawCount` within the requested limit.
- Complete, bounded raw-ID evidence: all IDs are valid snowflake strings, unique, and its count equals `rawCount`. Returned message IDs must belong to that evidence.
- When separate raw IDs are absent, mapped row IDs suffice only if `count(rows) = rawCount`; normalized item count is irrelevant.
- With an existing cursor, **every raw ID**, including filtered IDs, must be strictly newer. Compare decimal strings without floating-point conversion.
- Advance to the maximum raw ID for a nonempty proved page. An empty page retains the cursor.
- Persist progress only after the existing admission boundary confirms retained encounters and the checkpoint. Preserve coverage and retry semantics.

(己, p=0.99) Keep these negatives: missing/invalid IDs, inconsistent or truncated ID evidence, unknown raw count, older/equal hidden IDs, wrong source/account/channel, label transport failure, malformed retained items, and partial durable admission. The existing filtered fixture with `rawCount 2` but only one available ID remains a valid no-progress case. Full-page and valid empty-system-row expectations need the new behavior; malformed author/time/identity rejection remains intact.

The current runtime fixtures return synthetic tool details directly. They do not prove that the actual Discord tool preserves unfiltered IDs or distinguishes label failure. The refusal fixtures exercise the current throwing finalizer; they do not cover a normally returning finalizer or both refusal stages.

(己, p=1.0) This was read-only source and fixture inspection. I ran no tests, builds, jobs, native reviews, runtime/social/board operations, or thread actions. No future repair bytes are approved, and this assessment supplies no native approval.
